definition: NVIDIA's CUDA compiler driver. It splits a program into CPU code (passed to the host compiler) and GPU code, which it compiles to PTX and then to SASS machine code.
The real machine code of one NVIDIA GPU family (for example sm_90 for Hopper). The ptxas assembler turns PTX into SASS; unlike PTX, SASS for one generation generally does not run on the next.
The bundle a CUDA application ships: SASS machine code for each GPU generation it was built for, plus PTX that a newer driver can compile for GPUs that did not exist at build time.

Just-in-time compilation: turning code into machine instructions when a program loads or runs instead of ahead of time. The CUDA driver JIT-compiles PTX for new GPUs; Triton and DeepGEMM JIT-compile kernels for the exact shapes in use.
A group of up to 1,024 GPU threads that run on the same SM, share fast on-chip memory and can synchronise with each other. A kernel launch is a grid of thread blocks.
All the thread blocks created by one kernel launch. The hardware hands blocks to SMs as they free up, which lets the same code scale across GPUs of different sizes.
An ordered queue of GPU work (copies and kernel launches). Work in one stream runs in order; separate streams can overlap, which hides data transfers behind computation.
A CUDA feature that records a sequence of kernel launches once and replays it with a single launch, cutting CPU launch overhead - important for small, frequent inference steps.

Automatically benchmarking many versions of a kernel (tile sizes, pipeline depths, thread counts) on the actual hardware and shapes, then keeping the fastest. Used by cuBLAS heuristics, Triton and TorchInductor.

A family of attention kernels (v1 2022 to v4 2026) that compute attention in tiles held in on-chip memory instead of writing the full attention matrix to HBM. Each version was written first for NVIDIA GPUs.
The default compiler back end of PyTorch 2's torch.compile. It fuses operations and generates Triton kernels for GPUs and C++ for CPUs.
An open-source Python kernel language from the tile-ai project, used for DeepSeek's attention kernels. It targets NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm and Apple Metal and, since September 2026, Huawei Ascend 950.
